followup_reviews.Research finding: The shared 15 February 2023 measure remains one included parent with two post-specific phases. Later conflicting continuity claims remain visible instead of being converted into a single three-year closure. Keep the initial persons/cars/buses/light-freight restriction and the heavy-freight exception. The November Atameken continuation specifically concerns personal passage. Uzbek Syrdarya/Gulistan is not Kazakh Syrdarya–Malik. Both phases retain the exact shared onset and November last confirmation, held flags and no numeric durations. P1 has return reported by 24 March 2026, not on that exact first day; P2 has no observed reopening despite December commissioning. Retain broad Administration and service operation for explicitly stated reconstruction, modernisation and safety. No new political or security purpose is inferred. Daryo’s reported Customs Committee statement was freshly read. The initial official notice, indexed paired-post update, November interview and contradictory commissioning body were reread from fingerprinted receipts. The original Telegram post remains uninspected. Both phases remain unlocated. Propose separate post labels for P1 and P2 so neither unlocated phase appears to name both posts. No coordinates, geometry or temporal rule changes are proposed.
